card.name: Kalamatianos
card.era: Roots in antiquity; modern name from the town of Kalamata
card.profile: One of Greece's best-known dances, widely regarded as the national dance; danced in a chain/open circle, counterclockwise, dancers holding hands. Beat 7/8 subdivided 3+2+2 (slow-quick-quick); 12 steps over 4 bars (10 forward counterclockwise, 2 back). The lead dancer often holds the second by a handkerchief to perform elaborate steps and acrobatics. Inclusive (men, women, children); performed at weddings, festivals and diaspora gatherings, accompanied by clarinet, violin, laouto, drums and often bouzouki (English Wikipedia; Costa Navarino).
card.insight: Steps are identical to the syrtos but the meter differs (kalamatianos 7/8, syrtos 4/4); the kalamatianos is on Greece's National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage (a national, not UNESCO, recognition).
